tagline: Creating the future platform for growth
hero_kpi_rationale: Revenue is not directly reflected, but Gross Profit is the primary performance indicator in logistics services, capturing operational efficiency and market dynamics. The stability of this metric despite tight market conditions demonstrates DSV's operational resilience.

kpis.name: Gross Profit
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and the cost of logistics services, key to measuring commercial performance.
kpis.description: Gross Profit stands at DKK 42,974 million in 2024, down 1.2%, reflecting normalization after exceptional 2023 conditions.
kpis.signal: Gross Profit stable despite tight markets.

kpis.name: Operating Profit (excl. special items)
kpis.explanation: Profit after operating costs but before exceptional items such as acquisitions.
kpis.description: Operating Profit excluding special items reached DKK 16,096 million, down 8.4%, in line with expectations and reflecting normalization of market conditions.
kpis.signal: Expected decline after a very favorable 2023.

kpis.name: Adjusted Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated after investments, adjusted to reflect operational performance.
kpis.description: Adjusted Free Cash Flow declined to DKK 5,550 million in 2024, down 51.6%, impacted by normalization of market conditions after an exceptional 2023.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline due to cycle normalization.

kpis.name: Return on Invested Capital
kpis.explanation: Return generated on capital invested in the business.
kpis.description: ROIC declined from 17.8% to 15.4%, reflecting lower returns in a less favorable environment, while remaining solidly above industry standards.
kpis.signal: ROIC remains solid despite the decline.

kpis.name: Scope 1 & 2 Emissions Reduction
kpis.explanation: Percentage reduction in direct and indirect greenhouse gas emissions related to own operations.
kpis.description: DSV reduced Scope 1 & 2 emissions by 10.7% in 2024, driven by initiatives such as the Carbon Fee Fund, positioning the decarbonization roadmap favorably for 2030 targets.
kpis.signal: Significant emissions reduction through the Carbon Fee Fund.

kpis.name: Scope 3 Emissions Increase
kpis.explanation: Percentage increase in indirect emissions related to supplier, customer activities and logistics detours.
kpis.description: Scope 3 emissions increased 10.5% in 2024, primarily due to rerouting around Cape of Good Hope caused by Red Sea situation and increased global activity levels.
kpis.signal: Increase driven by higher activity and maritime rerouting caused by Red Sea situation.

kpis.name: Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the group following Schenker acquisition announced in September 2024: 73,000 DSV employees plus 86,600 Schenker employees.
kpis.description: DSV will employ approximately 160,000 people following completion of the Schenker acquisition announced in September 2024, transforming DSV into a global leader with more than double the current workforce (73,000 DSV employees plus 86,600 Schenker employees).
kpis.signal: Massive scale post-Schenker acquisition, becoming one of the world's largest players.

kpis.name: Scope 1 & 2 Emissions Reduction
kpis.explanation: Percentage reduction in direct and indirect greenhouse gas emissions related to own operations.
kpis.description: DSV reduced Scope 1 & 2 emissions by 10.7% in 2024, driven by initiatives such as the Carbon Fee Fund, positioning the decarbonization roadmap favorably for 2030 targets.
kpis.signal: Significant emissions reduction through the Carbon Fee Fund.

kpis.name: Schenker Acquisition
kpis.explanation: Transformative acquisition of Schenker announced in September 2024 for EUR 14.3 billion, creating a global logistics leader with approximately 160,000 combined employees.
kpis.description: In September 2024, DSV announced the acquisition of Schenker for EUR 14.3 billion (approximately DKK 107 billion), transforming DSV into a global leader with enhanced offerings across all three divisions and approximately 86,600 Schenker employees adding to DSV's base of 73,000 employees.
kpis.signal: Transaction larger than all previous DSV acquisitions combined, marking a major growth milestone.

risks.title: Complex Schenker integration
risks.score_rationale: Risk is highlighted in the 10-K with strong language ("landmark", "transform"). Trend is upward with recent acquisition announcement. Integrating an entity of this size represents major weight on industrial operations.

risks.title: Increased competition in European road market
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned in operational results with moderate to strong intensity language ("intense competition", "pressure on prices"). Trend is stable but persistent. Competition category is central to DSV's business model.

risks.title: Supplier dependence for road costs
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly cited in report with strong language ("significant cost pressure from suppliers"). Recurrent, therefore stable, and critical for Road division. Operational impact is high.

risks.title: Geopolitical disruptions in Red Sea
risks.score_rationale: Risk prominently featured in introduction with very strong language ("attacks on commercial ships", "longer transit times"). Trend is upward. Directly impacts maritime and air flows, key for DSV.

risks.title: Regulatory pressure on decarbonization
risks.score_rationale: Risk discussed in context of SBTi commitments and internal policies. Strong language ("net-zero commitment", "CO2 footprint on invoices"). Trend is upward. Environmental regulation weighs heavily on sector.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of integrated systems
risks.score_rationale: Risk implicit in IT strategy ("one main system per business area", "security"). While not highlighted as major risk, Schenker integration expands attack surface. Trend is upward. Critical for operational continuity.

risks.title: Dependence on Chinese e-commerce growth
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in introduction as growth driver ("Chinese e-commerce players exporting large volumes"). Positive language but reveals dependence. Trend is stable. Less critical than others but strategically important.

risks.title: Intensifying competition in contract solutions
risks.score_rationale: Risk mentioned in context of sector verticals and customized solutions. Moderate but recurring language. Trend is stable. Differentiation is crucial for organic growth.

ai_positioning.summary: DSV makes no mention of artificial intelligence strategy or initiatives in its 2024 annual report. Focus is on logistics efficiency, sustainability and Schenker integration, with no explicit reference to AI or cognitive technologies.
evidence: No mention of AI or machine learning in the annual report.
Innovations cited relate to digitalization of logistics solutions and integrated CO2 billing systems, not explicit AI.
R&D and technology initiatives focus on supply chain optimization and digital solutions with no reference to AI.
